name: Work
effects: Your Background also represents your professional abilities, something you can be paid for. When you Work, you gain Plugs equal to 1/10th the Starting income of your Background, plus your Tier.
text: Your Background also represents your professional abilities, something you can be paid for. When you Work, you gain Plugs equal to 1/10th the Starting income of your Background, plus your Tier.

name: Decipher
effects: When presented with either a cipher or a foreign language, and you have at least some reference regarding its solution, for example, a single translated word of the cipher, a hint from the maker, a similar language in common, etc. you may attempt to decode its meaning.

attrs.Collaboration: Skilled Collaborators roll a Chaos Die, and allow you to take the lower Die.
attrs.Time: Deciphering a single page-worth requires a number of Watches equal to the sum of two Chaos Dice, minus your Immanence.

text: When presented with either a cipher or a foreign language, and you have at least some reference regarding its solution, for example, a single translated word of the cipher, a hint from the maker, a similar language in common, etc. you may attempt to decode its meaning.

name: Conceptual Intuition
effects: You raise a Topic, which can be a place, a thing, a concept, especially something important to your current goals, aims, or circumstances. The GM will then roll Chaos Dice, equal to your Immanence. If any come up 6, you gain a Link, which is a vague association between the Topic and another, one which the GM knows is interesting or important.

attrs.Collaboration: Skilled Collaborators may contribute a Chaos Die, of all Collaborators' Dice, only the highest result it counted.
attrs.Structure: Links are just associations, a sense that one Topic is related to another, not so much a Clue but a promise of one. At most, a Link between Topics has a kind of vague shape to it, a feeling, emotional value, or gravity of import.
attrs.Time: Doing this takes one Watch, and is limited to once Daily. During the Watches of Twilight and Dawn you gain an effective Buff of 1 to your Immanence.

text: You raise a Topic, which can be a place, a thing, a concept, especially something important to your current goals, aims, or circumstances. The GM will then roll Chaos Dice, equal to your Immanence. If any come up 6, you gain a Link, which is a vague association between the Topic and another, one which the GM knows is interesting or important.

name: Recall
effects: You choose something you would have been able to witness, overhear, or may have incidentally noted in your past.

attrs.Collaboration: Skilled Collaborators can contribute a Chaos Die to the roll.
attrs.Procedure: The GM rolls Chaos Dice, up to twice your Immanence. If what you wish to remember occured within a number of Days equal to or less than the sum, you recall it.
attrs.Time: This requires a number of Minutes, up to the number of Days past minus your Immanence. You cannot retry this for the same thing within the same Day.
attrs.Limits: Recalled information is not exact, enough for a few words, an image, a face, etc. Each Chaos Die that rolls a 6 also distorts the recollection in some way.

text: You choose something you would have been able to witness, overhear, or may have incidentally noted in your past.

name: Practice Forms
summary: one motion, a thousand times over
effects: You obtain Practice equal to the Watches Spent, up to your Action. Practice can be spent increase any of your Melee Attacks by 1 (before or after rolling), or to instantly Maneuver 1 Meter as a 0 AP Reaction to anything at all.

attrs.Collaboration: Unskilled Collaborators can gain a single Practice for three Opportunity.

text: You obtain Practice equal to the Watches Spent, up to your Action. Practice can be spent increase any of your Melee Attacks by 1 (before or after rolling), or to instantly Maneuver 1 Meter as a 0 AP Reaction to anything at all.

name: Sport
effects: After participating in Sport, you gain a Buff to your Body or Reflex for the next Week, this is equal to the Watches spent, up to your Tier.

attrs.Collaboration: Unskilled Collaborators gain the same benefits but for half as long.
attrs.Relief: You can Coin-Flip to remove 1 Corruption after Sport, but must Rest before gaining this benefit again.

text: After participating in Sport, you gain a Buff to your Body or Reflex for the next Week, this is equal to the Watches spent, up to your Tier.

name: Hone Aim
effects: You gain Precision equal to the Watches spent, up to your Potence. Precision can be spent to increase a Ranged Attack by 1 (before or after rolling) or, conversely, to raise the Difficulty of any Attack against you or make it less Vicious. Precision can also be used when Striking with a Finesse Weapon to it more Vicious by one.

attrs.Collaboration: Unskilled Collaborators can gain a single Precision for three Opportunity.

text: You gain Precision equal to the Watches spent, up to your Potence. Precision can be spent to increase a Ranged Attack by 1 (before or after rolling) or, conversely, to raise the Difficulty of any Attack against you or make it less Vicious. Precision can also be used when Striking with a Finesse Weapon to it more Vicious by one.

name: Reckon the Odds
effects: Name a Foe you have witnessed previously and spend one Watch. For the next Day, you gain an Edge against them, which makes them Vulnerable to you equal to your Potence. At any time, you can Consume this Edge to force them to re-roll anything and take the result you choose.

attrs.Collaboration: Unskilled Collaborators who have witnessed a Foe can provide the necessary experience second-hand.

text: Name a Foe you have witnessed previously and spend one Watch. For the next Day, you gain an Edge against them, which makes them Vulnerable to you equal to your Potence. At any time, you can Consume this Edge to force them to re-roll anything and take the result you choose.

name: Conditioning
effects: You gain Strength for each Watch Spent, up to your Vitality. Strength can be spent at any time to shed a single point of Persistant or Standard Strain, or to temporary double your vertical lift for a single Full-Turn.

attrs.Collaboration: Unskilled Collaborators may gain 1 Strength for 3 Opportunity.
attrs.Liberation: If you spend three or more Opportunity at one time, you may Coin-Flip to shed one Corruption.

text: You gain Strength for each Watch Spent, up to your Vitality. Strength can be spent at any time to shed a single point of Persistant or Standard Strain, or to temporary double your vertical lift for a single Full-Turn.

name: First-Aid
effects: Interacting with an Injured Creature, you make a Vitality Test with a DC of 10+(their number of Injuries). This can be yourself, but this increases the DC by your Tier.

attrs.Collaboration: Skilled Collaborators grant a Boon.
attrs.Time: This is usually a 2_AP General Action, but can be extended for better odds. If you spend at least 6 AP you always end the Bleeding Condition, and one Minute or more grants a Boon to your Test.
attrs.Result: If you roll at least 8, you remove the Bleeding Condition, and Success removes a single Minor Injury.
attrs.Recovery Time: This can also hasten the Recovery Time of a Moderate or Treated Major Injury. Success against a DC of 10+(Injury Strain) you allow the Target to treat every Day that Week as two.

text: Interacting with an Injured Creature, you make a Vitality Test with a DC of 10+(their number of Injuries). This can be yourself, but this increases the DC by your Tier.

name: Reinforce
effects: You obtain Willpower, one for each Opportunity spent, up to your Resolve. Willpower can be spent to reduce the amount of Chaos Dice rolled for Panic Risk.

attrs.Collaboration: Unskilled Collaborators that participate may gain one Willpower for three Opportunity.

text: You obtain Willpower, one for each Opportunity spent, up to your Resolve. Willpower can be spent to reduce the amount of Chaos Dice rolled for Panic Risk.

name: Interrogate
effects: You attempt to extract some information from an unwilling Character, provided that they can Communicate with you and are in your Custody for the Duration.

attrs.Collaboration: Skilled Collaborators increase your Resolve by one.
attrs.Procedure: The GM secretly rolls Chaos Dice, two plus the Target's Resolve. The Duration required to obtain your answer is equal to the sum in Hours; for each 6, the Target will attempt to lie at some point in this process.
attrs.Custody and Time: You do not need to present for the entire Duration, but the Target must be held somewhere, prevented from leaving, to count as being in your Custody.
attrs.Forcing the Issue: For each Opportunity you are present, you reduce the Duration by Hours up to your Resolve. Likewise, you can double this efficacy by making things hard for the Target; the GM rolls another Chaos Die and subtracts it from the Duration, but a 6 yields another lie.

text: You attempt to extract some information from an unwilling Character, provided that they can Communicate with you and are in your Custody for the Duration.

name: Craft
effects: You attempt to create a non-Magical, non-Consumable, mundance Item, whether this is possible is adjudicated as follows:

attrs.Collaborators: Skilled Collaborators reduce the time needed by half, to a minimum of One Watch.
attrs.Nature: You must know how to make it and a plausible explanation why.
attrs.Resources: You must have the components, these usually have a Price around half that of the Object. When an Item is explicitely made of a given Resource, you must have have enough.
attrs.Time: Crafting an Item requires a number of Watches, 10 times its Tier, minus your Creation. So if your Tier was 3, a Tier_1 Item would take 7 Watches to Craft.
attrs.Limits: You cannot Craft an Item whose Tier exceeds your Creation.

text: You attempt to create a non-Magical, non-Consumable, mundance Item, whether this is possible is adjudicated as follows:

name: Patch
effects: You attempt to remove one Notch from an Item.

attrs.Collaborators: Skilled Collaborators increase your Creation by one.
attrs.Procedure:
Nature and Resources are evaluated as Crafting, and you must make a Creation Test depending on the time spent.
14
- 1 Hour:
12
- 1 Watch:
10
- 1 Day:
If you fail, you can spend more time to lower the DC. Success removes one Notch.

text: You attempt to remove one Notch from an Item.

name: Cook
summary: Comfort from some direction or other
effects:
You create a Meal for yourself and fellows, which can have Ingredient Traits with a sum Tier up to your 1+(your Creation), as follows:
You are immune to Extreme Cold of 1+T or below.
When Traveling on Foot, your Speed is greater by 5T
You are immune to Extreme Heat of 1+T or below.
You may ignore up to T Days of missed Sleep.
When rolling Terrain or Navigation Difficulty, you may reduce the amount of Chaos Dice by T.
All Traits can be added multiple times and may stack.

attrs.Collaborators: Each Collaborator cuts the time per Meal by 5 Minutes, to a minimum of 10.
attrs.Duration: A Meal for 6 or so Creatures takes 1 Hour to create, and the effects of a Meal last for the next 24 Hours.
attrs.Price: If you lack access to the Ingredients per say, they can be purchased with an approximate cost of T(1+T).
attrs.Unique Ingredients: You might gain access to an Ingredient which confers a special effect while at Sea. These can be included with a general Tier of 1, or more at GM discretion, as some may be simply harder to work with.

name: Scrounge
effects: You scrape the environs for anything of use, valuables, resources, and tools. If any whole Items exist, you find them unless concealed.

attrs.Collaboration: Skilled Collaborators may add their Opportunity to yours, and the Unskilled may do so at half the Rate half their spent Points to the total.
attrs.Scrap-Made: Further, when you Scrounge, you can assemble make-shift mundane Items. These scrap-made Items can be anything not Magical and must represent a base Item with a hypothetical Price no greater than (25 times Watches spent) in total. These Items must be intuitively plausible given the environment and account for Resources. For example, you cannot make a Canteen full of water in a desert, unless you find a spring, or fresh air Cannisters from nothing.

text: You scrape the environs for anything of use, valuables, resources, and tools. If any whole Items exist, you find them unless concealed.

name: Sea Travel
effects: You move from one place in the Shard Sea to another by Alembic Shard Ship. What remains uncertain is how long this may take, and what you may be required to spend.

attrs.Units: Expeditioners have a language of Sea-travel, ascending categories of greater and greater size. The Verdun nautical unit is the Maru, roughly 10 Sekta, 30 Koi, or 300 Kilometers in any Direction. On the Map of the Shard Sea, each Hex represents a space 30 Maru in Diameter.
attrs.Speed And Time: For each Day, a Ship moves up to 3(its Speed) Maru. This time is spent on the Ship, and doesn't require constant attention (especially if you have functioning crew). Expeditioners on a Ship may spend these Watches on other Activities for the Duration, unless circumstances demand their attention.
attrs.Depth: Traveling deeper is much faster, increasing Ship Speed by 2 for each Layer of the Sea descended below the Surface. However, the dangers below are rarely worth the risk. Ascending to the boarder of the Upper Aether reduces Speed by half, but is drastically safer.
attrs.Terrain and Navigation Difficulty: These concepts also apply to Sea Travel, though a little differently. Both are rolled in secret for each Stretch of the journey and, while Terrain Difficulty and Hazards apply in roughly the same fashion, Navigation Difficulty adds to the total Distance by 3 per 6 rolled.

text: You move from one place in the Shard Sea to another by Alembic Shard Ship. What remains uncertain is how long this may take, and what you may be required to spend.

name: Plot a Course
effects: Spend one Watch taking in your surroundings. You gain Guidance, up to one plus your Traversal. Guidance can be spent in the next 24 Hours to counter Navigation and Terrain Difficulty, each in their own ways.

attrs.Collaboration: Skilled Collaborators can increase your Traversal by 1.
attrs.Terrain: When you would roll Chaos Dice for Terrain Difficulty, you may spend Guidance to remove the same number of Dice.
attrs.Navigation: You do not necessarily know about Navigation Difficulty in advance, or when it effects your Travel. However, before moving one Hex, Guidance can be spent to counter one potential deflection from Navigation Difficulty.
attrs.Courses in the Sea: Guidance can also be used during Sea Travel, 3 can be spent to find a previously unknown Path, adding it to the array of choices for that Stretch of the Course.
attrs.Components: With instruments like Compass and Spyglass, you may gain one additional Guidance.

text: Spend one Watch taking in your surroundings. You gain Guidance, up to one plus your Traversal. Guidance can be spent in the next 24 Hours to counter Navigation and Terrain Difficulty, each in their own ways.

name: Overland Travel
effects: You choose one of the six Directions, corresponding to the faces of the current Hex, and Move by 1 Hex, marking the change on the Recorded Map.

attrs.Collaborators: Skilled Collaborators can confer a Boon to your Traversal Tests.
attrs.Terrain Difficulty: When Traveling, you roll Chaos Dice equal to the Terrain Difficulty of the current Hex. If any roll 6, a Travel Complication occurs, with a Severity given by the number of Dice. Terrain Complications are rolled by the GM and narrated to the Players, whose goal is to either resolve them or manage their consequences.
attrs.Navigation Difficulty: At the same time Players roll for Terrain Difficulty, the GM secretly rolls Chaos Dice equal to the Navigation Difficulty of those Hexes. You may roll Traversal to learn this, as well as the Terrain Difficulty of the Hex you would Travel to.
attrs.Speed and Time for Travel: Moving by foot, you may Travel one Hex (10 Kilimeters) per Watch. Other modes of transport can be had, and can impact the Distance moved, inferred from the new rate. For example, if one had mode of Travel that gave a Speed of 20km, they would move two Hexes within a Watch. Likewise, two Points would yield a Distance of three Hexes given a Speed of 15km.
attrs.Moving Multiple Hexes: Even when Traveling multiple Hexes at once, as outlined above, each Hex departed is evaluated individually, both for Direction and Terrain/Navigation Difficulty. For example, one could, with a Speed of 20 km, spend one Watch to move one Hex Northeast and then another Northwest.
attrs.Limits: A Shard's Aether Wake makes Overland Travel by Ship impossible, without a Pylon to stabilize the Aether within each Hex Travelled.

text: You choose one of the six Directions, corresponding to the faces of the current Hex, and Move by 1 Hex, marking the change on the Recorded Map.

name: Harvest
effects: You gather materials from your immediate vicinity, depending on the type.

attrs.Collaboration: Skilled Collaborators can add their Watches to yours, and the Unskilled can do so at half the rate.
attrs.Dead Creatures: From a freshly dead Creature, you may collect any natural poisons it may have had, its bones, organs, meat, etc. In general, you can obtain edibles equal to a Ration for every (10 minus your Traversal) Bulk. (Of course, this assumes the Creature is edible at all.) Each Creature may be Harvested for 30 Minutes per carcass. (1 Watch for 8.)
attrs.Consumable Flora: You obtain Doses up to your Traversal per Watch spent. A DC_10 Traversal Test can double this, triple for a Critical Success.
attrs.Resources: You obtain Bulk up to ten times your Traversal per Opportunity. A DC_10 Traversal Test can double this, triple for a Critical Success.
attrs.Limits: Of course, limited supplies are a factor, and the GM is free to limit Harvested resources to an amount logical for the Terrain.
attrs.Unique Harvests: At GM discretion, you might find something special, particularly if the Creature had a bounty, or was made of a naturally valuable material. This can often take more time to Harvest properly.

text: You gather materials from your immediate vicinity, depending on the type.

name: Animal Ken
effects:
You influence the demeaner and behavior of a non-verbal Creature like a Beast.
This measures the Target's animosity towards you. The GM knows this value.

attrs.Collaboration: Each Skilled Collaborator allows you to ignore a 6 over the whole course of the Activity.
attrs.Procedure: For every 2_AP spent, you can roll Chaos Dice up to one plus your Traversal. Each 1-3 raises its Disposition, while 4-6s reduce it, to a minimum of 1 (when it might begin to attack if it wasn't already). If its Disposition is more than 6, it ceases hostility. Targets trained to follow directions like mounts or companions are controlled by you in Initiative when their Disposition is greater than 6. (Training a wild animal for this usually takes a month or so of daily work, at least a Watch or so for each.)
attrs.Limits: Harming the Target or taking Actions of overt hostility towards it reduces its Disposition, as do sudden and frightening events, which cause temporary reductions even for trained companion Creatures. In those cases, you'll need to use Animal Ken to regain control of them.

text:
You influence the demeaner and behavior of a non-verbal Creature like a Beast.
This measures the Target's animosity towards you. The GM knows this value.

name: Disguise
effects: You create a Disguise, using clothing and perhaps specialized tools to pass its wearer off as someone else.

attrs.Collaboration: Skilled Collaborators can increase the resulting Quality by 1.
attrs.Plausibility: A Disguise needs to represent the Target (even if their is no real Target) in a believable way. Passing yourself off as an officer requires a uniform. The wearer must also reasonably resemble the Target, as even prosthetics may only do so much. When you create a Disguise, it has a Durability equal to the Hours spent, up to one plus your Darkness.
attrs.Using a Disguise: Whenever you pass yourself off as someone else, to one or more Creatures at a time, this counts as a use. When you use the Diguise, you roll a Chaos Die. A 6 Notches it; if this ever exceeds its Durability, the Disguise is seen through.

text: You create a Disguise, using clothing and perhaps specialized tools to pass its wearer off as someone else.

name: Safecrack
effects: You Interact with a Lock, and roll a Chaos Die for every 3 AP. Each 1 Notches it, unlocking once you exceed its Durability. Rolled 6s remove Notches.

attrs.Collaborators: Skilled Collaborators allow you to roll an additional Chaos Die.
attrs.Lock Tiers:
Locks have Durability along this general curve
Simple keylocks
- 1:
Houses
- 2:
A personal Safe
- 3:
Bank vaults
- 6:
attrs.Skill: You may roll more Chaos Dice when Safecracking, up to your Darkness.

text: You Interact with a Lock, and roll a Chaos Die for every 3 AP. Each 1 Notches it, unlocking once you exceed its Durability. Rolled 6s remove Notches.

name: Cover Tracks
effects: The GM rolls a secret Test using your Darkness. On a success, you erase forensic evidence of your presence from a location, along a path, etc.

attrs.Collaborators: Skilled Collaborators reduce the Difficulty by 1, Unskilled by half that amount.
attrs.Difficulty:
This depends on how much evidence you need to remove, corresponding with your relation to the place:
14
- Your own home:
12
- Residence of at least a Day:
10
- Present for only one Scene:
attrs.Degrees of Failure: If you fail by less than your Darkness, the GM will tell you. Otherwise, your success is ambiguous until consequences ensue.
attrs.Critical effect: The GM will tell you that you succeeded.
attrs.Multiple Traces: You can erase the evidence of several people, but each additional Creature raises the DC by 1.
attrs.Time:
This can be performed on the move, but you can spend Opportunity in a single place to gain Boons to this roll at a rate of one for one.
General Activity Sneak
You attempt to take an Action or Actions without being Detected. All Actions while Sneaking are declared before rolling, and occur after the pool is rolled.
attrs.Visibility: Sneaking automatically fails if you do not start in Cover from your Witnesses. Witnesses mean Creatures that would matter were they to see you. Your Allies, a hapless onlooker with some Scopes, or a passing bird are not usually relevant Witnesses.
attrs.Risk:
The GM will secretly roll a Pool of Chaos Dice, and if any come up Face 6, you are Detected. The size of this Pool is determined by the following conditions:
4
2
1
- Exposure| Clear:  | Murky:  | Dark:
This identifies how easily the Witness could perceive you, loud, badly lit, or close environs are usually Dark and just about any fight is usually Murky. Clear conditions are just the worst possible situation to be Sneaking.
-
The Pool size is increased by the Luminance of the most Skilled single Witness to your Actions.
- Witnesses|
The Pool size is decreased by your own Darkness, to a minimum of one.
- Skill|
Each Action after the first increases the Pool by one.
- Multiplicity:
attrs.Results: If none of the Dice come up 6, your Actions resolve without Detection. These may cross through the Senses of any Creature with no consequence, but they would instantly Detect you if you were to end your Sneaking there. So, you might Sneak to Move into Engagement from Total Cover and Attack an unsuspecting Foe, denying them the chance to Resist. After the Attack Resolved, you would be Detected; instead, if you Snuck to Move, Attack, and Moved again, you might leave Engagement and return to Cover, starting and ending Undetected (at the cost of a higher potential Risk of being Detected in the first.)

text: The GM rolls a secret Test using your Darkness. On a success, you erase forensic evidence of your presence from a location, along a path, etc.

name: Deceive
effects:
You attempt to lead a Target astray, to lie and mislead.
This measures how the Target feels about you. NPC Dispotions are only known to the GM.
This measures how subjectively plausible the Target regards the lie, and is known by the GM.

attrs.Collaborators: Each Skilled Collaborator raises the maximum Dice you can roll by one.
attrs.Procedure: First, roll a Chaos Die as you make your case to the NPC in-Character. You can roll more for each Minute you spend. Rolling a 1-3 raises their Attitude, and a 4-6 decreases it. If their Attitude would be more than 6, they are Deceived. If their Attitude would fall below 1, they break off the conversation and flatly deny you.
attrs.Limits: You can only roll Chaos Dice up to the Disposition of the NPC plus your own Darkness, and automatically fail if you attempt to exceed it. The Target can also pretend to believe you.
attrs.Extra Factors: If you make an especially good point, or merit it by circumstance, the GM will notify you that the Disposition of the NPC was increased by 1. These changes can be lasting at their discretion, carrying into further interactions as the Target's opinion of you increases.

text:
You attempt to lead a Target astray, to lie and mislead.
This measures how the Target feels about you. NPC Dispotions are only known to the GM.
This measures how subjectively plausible the Target regards the lie, and is known by the GM.

name: Intimidation
effects:
You communicate, for 1_AP, the danger of crossing you, forcefully.
This measures how threatened the Target is by you. The GM knows this, but if your Tiers are equal, this is usually 3; circumstances and reputation are big factors.

attrs.Collaboration: Skilled Collaborators grant you one Boon, and can participate as a 1_AP Reaction.
attrs.Procedure: Make a Darkness Test with a DC=16-(Their Disposition). If you succeed, they refrain from taking any hostile Actions (or anything you explicitely forbid), so long as you don't attempt to harm them. If you Critically Succeed, they attempt to flee the Scene; or they might even fight for you, so long as their close loyalties aren't crossed.
attrs.Contagion: If multiple Foes perceive this, and their Disposition would be higher than the Target's, they are also Intimidated on a success. You can ask your Gm to point out group-leaders with a DC_10 Luminance to game this interaction.
attrs.Context and Limits:
If you've killed or Injured one the Target's Allies in the same Scene, you roll with a Boon. If you've attemped and failed to Intimidate them, you suffer a Bane. Targets are immune to a third attempt after two failures.
-
Mindless Creatures and those incapable of language like Beasts are immune to Intimidation as such.

name: Study
effects: You attempt to ascertain some information from available Sources, be it a single book, a library, or an entire college. To evaluate this, clearly specify a Question to the GM. They will then roll a secret Test using your Luminance to arrive at the result.

attrs.Collaboration: Trained Collaborators can pool their Watches and share the benefits of Study.
attrs.Results: With a roll of at least 10, you gain a loose picture of the body of information available in the Source, as well as a general answer to the Question. At 12 or more, you gain a fairly exact answer to the Question. On a roll of 14, you gain a precise answer.
attrs.Time: Study takes at least one Watch, and each additional adds a Boon to your Test.
attrs.Failure: If you fail, you do not learn whether the answer exists in the Source, and the GM will provide a generic, but wrong answer to the Question. If the roll is a natural 2, this misinformation will be extremely specific, and in the complete wrong direction.
attrs.Critical effect: The GM will reveal your roll.

text: You attempt to ascertain some information from available Sources, be it a single book, a library, or an entire college. To evaluate this, clearly specify a Question to the GM. They will then roll a secret Test using your Luminance to arrive at the result.

name: Wayfinding
effects: You make a Luminance Test against the Navigation Difficulty of the current Terrain (a value which remains undisclosed.) If you succeed, the GM indicates your current location using the best information available to your Character. If you have a Map which represents the location, for example, you could learn your position on it. If not, you might learn at least relative Distances from important or visited landmarks.

attrs.Collaboration: Skilled Collaborators add a Boon to this Test.
attrs.Land and Sea: This works about the same when in the Sea or exploring a Shard. However, you must have a functioning Aetheric Wavecaster to use this in the Sea.
attrs.Duration and Difficulty: When Wayfinding, the GM rolls Chaos Dice equal to the Navigation Difficulty. The sum, in Minutes, is the time taken to complete this Activity, and each 6 raises the Difficulty by 1.
attrs.Critical effect:
This reduces the Duration to 6 Seconds.
General Activity Surveying
Make a Luminance Test, and gain the following information, all of which should be noted on the Recorded Map of the region.
attrs.General Shard Terrain: You automatically learn the Size, shape, and all Imminent Terrain of a Shard that you can see. When approaching in a Ship, this ranges over the whole Shard. When doing so on the Shard itself, elevation greater than your current locale can block this unless circumvented.
attrs.Obscure and Hidden Terrain:
When on land, You may also discover Obscure or even hidden Terrain, depending on the roll:
Compare the Test to the DC:(8 plus the Navigation Difficulty) of all adjacent Hexes. Success reveals Obscure Terrain there. Hexes further away can also be Surveyed from greater elevation, with an increase of 2 to the DC, per 10km of Distance.
- Obscure Terrain:
Compare the Test to DC:(10 plus the Navigation Difficulty) of the current Hex. Success reveals Hidden Terrain there.
- Hidden Terrain:
attrs.Time: You can perform this Activity within 10 Minutes, inflicting a Bane on the Test, or spend more time for a Bonus of 1 per Watch.
attrs.Critical Effect: A natural 12 increases the effective roll by 3.
attrs.GM Fiat: The GM may use this Activity to drop hints about your current environ and those nearby, especially about the Ecosystem there.

text: You make a Luminance Test against the Navigation Difficulty of the current Terrain (a value which remains undisclosed.) If you succeed, the GM indicates your current location using the best information available to your Character. If you have a Map which represents the location, for example, you could learn your position on it. If not, you might learn at least relative Distances from important or visited landmarks.

name: Forecast
effects: Spend one Watch and make a Luminance Test; you gain the locations of any Sea Ripples within the current Hex, depending on your roll.

attrs.Collaboration: Skilled Collaborators can add a Boon to your Test.
attrs.Ripples: Ripples originate from macro-scopic or especially 'loud' disturbances in the Sea. When you Forecast, the GM will consult their Objective Map of the local Sea and report how many, where, and how far away a given Ripple is. Keep in mind, this does not reveal the actual nature of the Ripple, though many Ripples come with clues.
attrs.Ripples in Other Hexes: You may also Forecast to other Hexes in the Shard Sea. When doing so, you indicate the Hex and your roll is penalized by the Distance in Sea Hexes.
attrs.Mapping the Sea: When you Forecast a Ripple, the Distance you obtain is relative to your current place in the Sea. This can be mapped by drawing a line to the Ripple and writing the Distance on the line-segment. Repeatedly doing so and from multiple locations will build up a Recorded Map of the local Sea over time. Of course, these are only guesses, and only good for so long, as things are prone to drifting.
attrs.Critical effect: If you roll a natural 12, your rolled result is increased by 6.

text: Spend one Watch and make a Luminance Test; you gain the locations of any Sea Ripples within the current Hex, depending on your roll.

name: Convince
effects:
You attempt to convince a Target to do or believe something.
This measures how the Target feels about you. NPC Dispotions are only known to the GM.
This measures how they feel the subject you'd like to Convince them of. Like Dispositions, this is only known by the GM.

attrs.Collaborators: Each Skilled Collaborator raises the maximum Dice you can roll by one.
attrs.Procedure: First, roll a Chaos Die as you make your case to the NPC in-Character. You can roll more for each Minute you spend. Rolling 1-3 or less raises their Attitude, and a 4-6 decreases it. If their Attitude would be more than 6, they are Convinced. If their Attitude would fall below 1, they break off the conversation and flatly refuse.
attrs.Limits: You can only roll Chaos Dice up to the Disposition of the NPC plus your own Unity, and automatically fail if you attempt to exceed it. Because this is a hidden value, Convincing is a bit of a gamble. Likewise, the Target can always lie, entertaining you for as long as they wish, or pretending to be Convinced.
attrs.Extra Factors: If you make an especially good point, or merit it by circumstance, the GM will notify you that the Disposition of the NPC was increased by 1. These changes can be lasting at their discretion, carrying into further interactions as the Target's opinion of you increases.

Finding Mentors

name: Make a Plan
effects: Spend at least one Watch. You record a specific Plan, a sequence of Actions taken in Initiative by Members (Yourself and Allies) up to your Tactics.

attrs.Collaboration: Members of the Plan must Collaborate. If Trained, they can pool their total spent Opportunity towards the effective total.
attrs.Specificity: Plans identify the exact Actions taken in Initiative, assuming a simultaneous Turn for all Members and their order. For example, 'John Grabs the Target I point to, then Suzette Shoots them.' If the sequence cannot take place, owing to a lack of AP, of specific Targets, or lack of a Member in a Plan, you cannot Execute it. If such an impossibility becomes the case during a Plan, it ends.
attrs.Duration: When Making a Plan, the total AP called for cannot exceed twice the Watches spent Making it. During its simultaneous Turn, Members of a Plan have 3 AP to spend for its sequence of events, even if they otherwise wouldn't (from the Stunned Condition, for example).
attrs.Executing a Plan: At any time, you may Execute your Plan as a Reaction, instantly bringing all of its Members into one simultaneous Turn at the present Initiative (as if you had Preempted the current Turn.) Then, the Plan either takes place exactly as specified, or ends when its sequence is broken/becomes impossible to carry out.
attrs.Duration and Aftermath: Foes can still React to a Plan, but this does not break it unless the effect of the Reaction does so as outlined above. More importantly, the simultaneous Turn of a Plan cannot be interrupted in any other way than Reactions while it remains in effect. Members in a Plan return to their previous places in the Turn Order after it has taken place, including yourself.
attrs.Limits:
if you were a Member in your own Plan, Execution counts as a Primary Action for you. Further, you may only have a number of Plans up to your Tactics at any time. After Executing one, it is Consumed and must be Planned again.
Feat 1: Coordination
Tactics is the study of sequences and people, collecting a disorganized mob and transforming them into a machine.
When you Flank, you can Coin-Flip to make the Target Off_Balance for 1 Simple-Turn.
Feat 2: Prediction
Foreknowledge is divine. You might call yourself a secular authority on the subject.
You make a verbal (out loud) Prediction about an Enemy, such as "they will Attack (so and so)" or "you will Interact with (such and such)". If they follow your Prediction, they become Off_Balance for 1 Full-Turn.
Feat 3: Group Action
Plans have a flow, a tidal current that can bolster the, efforts of all involved.
Members of your Plan gain a Boon which they can spend on Test made for its Duration.
Feat 4: Call Out
Few things are as troubling as being read.
When your Prediction is successful, the Target Risks Minor Panic. If they already were the Target of a successful Prediction, this is Moderate instead.
Feat 5: Double Time
Under your instruction, the collective machinery of the group operates at maximal efficiency.
When you Execute a Plan, you can Coin Flip to keep it, instead of Consuming the Plan.
Feat 6: Demoralize
Effective jibes and clever words are often as deadly as any sword in a fight.
When your Prediction is successful, you can Taunt them as a 1 AP Reaction. Taunting an Enemy provokes Minor Panic Risk from them, regardless of how many times you have already Predicted them. Each Taunt after the first increases the Severity of this Risk.

summary: With the Voice, then the Soul. We swear our fealty.
effects:
You seek the aid of a Spirit willing to enjoin and dwell with you.
Mitha are simple beings and need only be Named in the Rite to Bind them.
Akthe must agree to dwell with you to be Bound, in addition to their Bond. Many of the more willfull Akthe with demand tasks and services before consenting to this.
Each Mitha you would Bind or release takes one Minute, Binding or releasing an Akthe as a Familiar takes one Watch.

summary: To Justice, the form and order of oaths. We Swear our hearts.
effects:
The means of Creating Magic Items, one of the most valuable sorts of commodity in Anya territory and beyond.
This indexes into the Artifice and Magic Items rules from Shards of Life. These Items use the same rules, but Spirit Binding subs for Artifice, Plugs are subbed for Light from your stores, and Spirit Names are subbed for analogous Runes.
When Crafting or inventing Magic Items, only your Bound Spirits may be called on. This concern does not apply to using Magic Items already made.
